chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi from al-Husayn ibn 'Ilwan from 'Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). He said: I asked my father, the Master of Worshipers (peace be upon him),

and I said to him: O father! Inform me about our grandfather, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): When he ascended to heaven and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him with fifty prayers, why did he not ask Him for a reduction for his community until Moses son of 'Imran (peace be upon him) said to him: Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction, for your community cannot bear that?

So he said: O my son! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) does not make suggestions to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, nor does he return to Him regarding anything He commands him. So when Moses (peace be upon him) asked him that and became an intercessor for his community with Him, it was not permissible for him to reject the intercession of his brother Moses (peace be upon him). So he returned to his Lord asking Him for a reduction, until it was reduced to five prayers.

He said: So I said to him: O father! Then why did he not return to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him for a reduction from five prayers, when Moses (peace be upon him) had asked him to return to his Lord and ask Him for a reduction? So he said: O my son! He (peace be upon him and his family) wished to secure for his community the reduction along with the reward of fifty prayers, due to the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like' [6:160].

Do you not see that when he (peace be upon him and his family) descended to earth, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came down to him and said: O Muhammad! Your Lord conveys greetings to you and says: 'They are five [counting as] fifty. My word is not changed, and I am not unjust to the servants.'

He said: So I said to him: O father! Is it not the case that God, exalted be His remembrance, is not described with a place? So he said: Indeed, God is exalted above that. So I said: Then what is the meaning of the saying of Moses (peace be upon him) to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): Return to your Lord? So he said: Its meaning is the meaning of the saying of Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Surely I am going to my Lord; He will guide me' [37:99], and the meaning of the saying of Moses (peace be upon him): 'I have hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased' [20:84], and the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'So flee to God' [51:50]—meaning, make pilgrimage to the House of God.

O my son! The Ka'ba is the House of God; whoever makes pilgrimage to the House of God has directed himself toward God. The mosques are the houses of God; whoever goes to them has gone to God and directed himself toward Him. The one who prays, for as long as he is in his prayer, stands before God, Glorious is His Majesty. The people at the station of 'Arafa stand before God, Mighty and Majestic. And God, Blessed and Exalted, has places in His heavens; whoever is raised to a place therein has been raised to Him. Have you not heard God, Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him' [70:4]? And He says, Mighty and Majestic, in the story of 'Isa (peace be upon him): 'Rather, God raised him to Himself' [4:158]. And He says, Mighty and Majestic: 'To Him ascend goodly words, and righteous deeds raise them' [35:10].

key_terms.التَّخْفِيف: Reduction/lightening (of the prayer obligation from fifty to five)
key_terms.الْمِعْرَاج: The Night Ascension of the Prophet to the heavens
key_terms.سَيِّد الْعَابِدِين: Master of Worshipers, honorific title of Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sajjad
key_terms.شَفَاعَة: Intercession; here Moses's intercession on behalf of the Muslim community
key_terms.يَقْتَرِح: To suggest, propose, or make requests of one's own accord

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet not ask God to reduce prayers from fifty during the Mi'raj?
ai.summary: This hadith records a dialogue between Zayd ibn 'Ali and his father Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (al-Sajjad), the fourth Imam, on the occasion of the Mi'raj (Night Ascension). Zayd asks why the Prophet Muhammad did not himself request the reduction of the fifty daily prayers, and the Imam explains that the Prophet never makes suggestions to God but could not refuse Moses's intercession. The hadith then addresses a deeper theological question: how could Moses tell the Prophet to 'return to his Lord' if God has no physical location? The Imam explains that expressions like 'going to God' or 'returning to God' refer to orientation toward sacred spaces—the Ka'ba, mosques, and places of worship—where one stands in the presence of God.
word_analysis: returns to Him/refers back to Him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Muhammad b. `Isam (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ya`qub al-Kulayni narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Muhammad narrated to us from Muhammad b. Sulayman from Isma`il b. Ibrahim from Ja`far b. Muhammad al-Tamimi from al-Husayn b. `Ilwan from `Amr b. Khalid from Zayd b. `Ali (as). He said: I asked my father, the Master of Worshipers (as),

and I said to him: O father! Inform me about my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s): When he ascended to heaven, and his Lord commanded him to do fifty prayers, why did he not ask Him to lighten the load on his Nation until Musa b. `Imran (as) told him: "Return to your Lord and ask him to lighten the load, for surely, your Nation cannot fulfill this"?

So, he said: O my son! Surely, the Messenger of Allah (s) would not make suggestions to his Lord, nor would he return to Him with regards to something He had commanded him. So, when Musa (as) asked him, he became the intercessor of his Nation through him, and [thus] he was unable to reject the intercession of his brother Musa (as) (i.e. Musa interceded on behalf of the Muslim Nation, and the Prophet was unable to reject the plea of Musa). So, he returned to his Lord to ask him to lighten the burden, until it became five prayers.

He said: So, I said to him: O father! Then why did he not return to his Lord to lighten it to less than five prayers, for Musa (as) told him to return to his Lord [again] to ask him to lighten it [further]? So, he said: O my son! He (s) wanted to lighten the burden on his Nation through the reward of fifty prayers, as Allah says, "He who comes with a good deed will have ten like it." [6:160]

When he (s) descended to the Earth, Gabriel (as) came down to him and said: "O Muhammad! Surely, your Lord recites the salaam to you, and says: 'Surely, they are five [prayers worth] fifty. My words have not been exchanged, and I am not oppressive to the worshipers.'"

He said: So, I said to him: O father! Isn't it the case that Allah is not described with a place? So, he said: Of course. May Allah be exalted above that. So, he said: So, what is the meaning of the saying of Musa (as) to the Messenger of Allah (s): "Return to your Lord"? So, he said: Its meaning is the [same] meaning as the saying of Ibrahim (as): "Surely, I am going to my Lord for guidance" [37:99], and the meaning of the saying of Musa (as): "I hasten to You, my Lord, so that You may be pleased." [20:84], and His saying, "So, hasten to Allah" [50:51] - meaning, make pilgrimage to the House of Allah.

O my son! The Ka`ba is the House of Allah. Whoever makes pilgrimage to the House of Allah has made his intention toward Allah. The mosques are the houses of Allah, so whoever goes to them has gone to Allah and made his intention toward Him. The one who prays stands before Allah for the duration of his prayer. Those who stand at `Arafa stand before Allah. Surely, for Allah there are places in His heavens; whoever ascends to a place of His therein has ascended to Him. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, "The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him" [70:4]? He says in the story of `Isa (as), "Rather, Allah raised him to Himself" [4:158], and He says, "Goodly words ascend to Him and righteous deeds are raised up by Him" [35:10].
